title: PhysxParticleAPI (particle object base)
summary: Base API of a particle object, applied automatically by USD with PhysxParticleSetAPI. The parser never checks it: its columns are read on every prim that lists PhysxParticleSetAPI, and its presence only steers property changes, where a PointInstancer that lists it is not handled as a rigid-body instancer.

columns.name: physxParticle:particleSystem
columns.absent: The set has no particle system: the runtime logs 'PhysX Particles at <path> are missing a valid simulation-owner particle system and will not be simulated.' and creates nothing. Only the first target is used.
columns.notes: The set takes its scene and the system's resolved solidRestOffset and fluidRestOffset from this target. The ovstage walker also parses a target system that its own PhysxParticleSystem enumeration did not reach.

columns.name: physxParticle:particleEnabled
columns.absent: true. With false the set is created but its particle buffer is not added to the particle system.
columns.notes: On change the property update enables or disables the set.

columns.name: physxParticle:selfCollision
columns.absent: false: the set's particle phase lacks the PhysX self-collide flag, so its particles do not interact with particles of the same group. USD's fallback is true, so write the value.
columns.notes: On change the property update sets or clears the flag on every particle phase of the set.

columns.name: physxParticle:particleGroup
columns.absent: Group 0. The group selects the PhysX phase of the set's particles; the runtime creates one phase per group and particle system, with the system's PBD material.
columns.notes: On change the property update rewrites the group bits (eParticlePhaseGroupMask) of every particle phase of the set.

interactions.rule: The columns are read in the particle-set parse, which is gated on PhysxParticleSetAPI alone; USD lists this API automatically with it.

Live edits of positions, orientations, velocities, angularVelocities, protoIndices and ids on a PointInstancer are handled as rigid-body instancer changes only when the instancer does not list this API; a protoIndices or ids edit there is a structural change. A populator that lists PhysxParticleSetAPI on a PointInstancer should therefore list this API too, as USD applies it automatically with PhysxParticleSetAPI.
